original_sql:
SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name
FROM customer c
WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey) > 20

candidates.sql: SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name FROM customer c JOIN (SELECT o_custkey FROM orders GROUP BY o_custkey HAVING COUNT(*) > 20) o ON c.c_custkey = o.o_custkey
candidates.rationale: Converts the correlated subquery into a join with a subquery that groups orders by customer key and filters for those with more than 20 orders.

candidates.sql: SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name FROM customer c WHERE c.c_custkey IN (SELECT o_custkey FROM orders GROUP BY o_custkey HAVING COUNT(*) > 20)
candidates.rationale: Replaces the correlated subquery with an IN clause that uses a subquery to find customer keys with more than 20 orders.

candidates.sql: SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name FROM customer c JOIN orders o ON c.c_custkey = o.o_custkey GROUP BY c.c_custkey, c.c_name HAVING COUNT(o.o_orderkey) > 20
candidates.rationale: Joins the customer and orders tables and groups by customer key and name, filtering for those with more than 20 orders.

candidates.sql: SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name FROM customer c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey GROUP BY o.o_custkey HAVING COUNT(*) > 20)
candidates.rationale: Replaces the correlated subquery with an EXISTS clause that uses a subquery to check for the existence of more than 20 orders for each customer.

candidates.sql: SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name FROM customer c WHERE c.c_custkey IN (SELECT o_custkey FROM orders GROUP BY o_custkey HAVING COUNT(*) > 20) ORDER BY c.c_custkey
